reuse.why: All providers share the new link guard, and Fintegra reuses bank selection, synchronization and response handling, though local unlink cleanup remains copied.

duplication.why: Fintegra duplicates an existing linking workflow and transaction downloader, while takeover duplicates the local cleanup in unlinkAccount.

placement.why: Provider integration follows the existing module boundaries, but an assertion-named helper now also mutates account links.

scope.why: The edits stay focused on the four requested linking changes and their supporting types, configuration and release notes.

maintainability.why: Centralized linking rules help maintenance, but copied provider workflows and mutation hidden inside validation create avoidable coupling.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Existing bank-selection and sync abstractions are used; unlinkAccount includes remote cleanup and does not expose a reusable local-only operation.

disguised_duplication.where: linkFintegraAccount and downloadFintegraTransactions reproduce existing provider implementations with provider names and endpoint details substituted.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked gains replaceExistingLink and combines duplicate rejection, target validation and destructive takeover; its four conditional branches handle conflict rejection, upgradingId, closed targets and conditionally missing targets.
